newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB seen posting 13 pct rise in H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: AIB seen posting 13 pct rise in H1 profits.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc is expected to announce an increase of at least 13 percent in pre-tax profits when it releases half-year results on Thursday.

Analysts say the strength of the Irish economy, a better-than-expected performance from AIB's U.S. operations and the contribution from Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy, the Polish bank in which AIB holds a 60 percent stake, should be the main factors driving growth.
Davy Stockbrokers is forecasting half-year pre-tax profits of 232 million Irish pounds, up from 201 million in the first half of 1996.
The broker is looking for earnings per share of 21.3 pence against 18.3 pence last time.

"Vigorous growth in domestic lending, a strong focus on fee-based income and a higher contribution from WBK should combine to drive strong growth in PBT (profits before tax) and EPS at the half-way stage," Davy said.
Irish double digit lending growth continued through the first half of 1997 and should be a major factor underpinning the results, analysts say.

The bank's U.S. subsidiary, First Maryland Bancorp (FMB) also performed well in the first half with strong loan growth and strong fee growth while expenses were contained, said Oliver O'Shea, analyst at Goodbody, who forecasts pre-tax profits of 229 million.
FMB recently announced an 11.7 percent increase in first-half earnings to $69.9 million.
The figures should also be boosted by a bigger-than-expected Polish contribution after AIB raised its stake in WBK to 60.2 percent from 45.7 percent earlier this year.
With the interim dividend already declared, analysts say the main focus will be on AIB's proposed buyback of up to 50 million shares.

As part of its acquisition of Dauphin Deposit Corp, AIB offered Dauphin shareholders cash or AIB American Depositary Receipts and said it would seek shareholder approval to buy up to 50 million of its shares in the open market.
"With the dividend already known, the main interest will be in details of the buyback," said Riada analyst Eamon Hughes who is forecasting pre-tax profits of 228 million.
AIB previously announced that it would pay an interim dividend of 6.8 pence per share, an increase of 14.3 percent on 1996.
The dividend was declared ahead of the half-year results because of the bank's acquisition of Dauphin.
